verdict.rationale: Carta's API docs show first-class objects for the entire cap table: capitalization tables by share class, stakeholders, option grants (including draft grants awaiting board approval), convertible notes/SAFEs, and 409A fair market values, all exposed as a queryable data source that other apps and audits can read from (carta-docs-18–23, carta-docs-10). This matches the core of the story that a founder's cap table (share classes, SAFEs, options, certificates) lives centrally and can be relied on programmatically by third parties like auditors. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on corroboration that investors and auditors actually treat Carta as a trusted single source of truth in practice, and explicit product documentation (vs. API reference) describing certificate/audit workflows; community evidence in the pack focuses on sales/cancellation complaints rather than cap-table data integrity, so it neither confirms nor disputes accuracy claims.
